text: Q/P scope cross-check: Q studies private locations and mechanisms that approximately minimize maximum/social cost while eliciting locations strategy-proofly; its abstract reports, inter alia, a best-possible deterministic 2-approximation for line/general/max cost and a deterministic 2-approximation for circle/max cost. P studies commitment to cooperation in a spatial-temporal bargaining/navigation game and compares formal contracts that compile to code with natural contracts that require reinterpretation, finding self-negotiated contracts can improve cooperation. Thus P supports a representation/enforcement manipulation, but not yet a facility-location or truthful-revelation claim.

I reject the abstract-scan proposal as currently phrased. Measuring whether LLMs truthfully report does not by itself test or preserve Q strategy-proofness: strategy-proofness is a property of the implemented outcome rule and preferences (truthful reporting is a dominant strategy), not a behavioral truth-frequency claim. P targets commitment/defection after negotiated agreement, a different failure mode. Also Q approximation guarantees are theorem-specific (objective, domain, deterministic/randomized); they cannot be referred to generically as Q approximation guarantees.

Sharpened publication hypothesis: contract representation creates an implementation gap in strategy-proof mechanism design. Encode one precisely specified Q mechanism in (i) an executable formal contract whose allocation is mechanically fixed and (ii) a natural contract reinterpreted by an LLM. On a preregistered finite location/report grid, enumerate unilateral misreports and compute ex-post incentive regret using true-location nearest-facility costs, plus the mechanism-specific approximation ratio against the true optimum. Validate the compiled condition against the Q rule as a control. A supported non-obvious result would be that reinterpretation makes the effective allocation mapping context/model-dependent, producing positive deviation regret and violations of Q bound even when the natural text is extensionally intended to specify the same rule; alternatively, equivalence/null results are informative if powered across interpreters.

Do not make self-negotiation the primary independent variable. Allowing agents to negotiate mechanism terms changes the mechanism/game and confounds representation fidelity with bargaining. Hold substantive Q rule fixed across formal versus natural representations; if negotiation is studied, separate it as a second factorial manipulation. Distinguish semantic implementation audit (same reports -> same facility distribution), incentive audit (max gain from unilateral misreport), and behavioral audit (LLM report choices). Only the first two bear directly on preservation of Q guarantees.

Evidence limitation/unresolved: inputs/Q.txt and inputs/P.txt contain titles and abstracts only, and the ledger had no substantive partner entries at read time (latest 0). Exact mechanism definitions, assumptions, contract enforcement/compiler details, and experimental protocols are unavailable, so the proposed experiment is conditional on obtaining full texts and selecting one Q theorem/mechanism. The strongest current line is an implementation-fidelity result, not a claim that contracting induces honesty.
ready at #5

Cross-check with Ada: Q states agents have private locations, cost is expected distance to the nearest facility, and mechanisms should elicit information truthfully “(i.e., strategy-proof)”; its guarantees are separated by domain/objective/randomization (e.g. deterministic 2-approximation for line/general/max cost, randomized 5/3 for line/special/max cost, deterministic 2 for circle/max cost). P says representations range from formal contracts “that compile to code” to natural contracts “that require reinterpretation,” and reports improved cooperative outcomes. These passages support a representation-fidelity experiment, but P supplies no evidence about truthful revelation or approximation preservation.

Agreement with Ada #2/#4, sharpening the rejection: the scan’s proposed dependent variable conflates observed truth-telling with dominant-strategy incentive compatibility. An LLM may lie under a genuinely strategy-proof rule (weak dominance/ties or model error), or tell truth under a manipulable implementation. Likewise, self-negotiation changes the allocation rule rather than merely its representation. Therefore neither truth frequency nor negotiated contracts can be the primary test of whether Q’s theorem survives implementation.

Single publication-grade hypothesis: a natural-language rendition of one fixed Q facility-location mechanism induces an interpreter-dependent effective mechanism, whereas a compiled formal rendition preserves the specified mapping. On a finite report grid, first audit extensional equivalence for every report profile (including randomized output distributions); then compute ex-post unilateral deviation regret under Q’s nearest-facility cost and the exact theorem-specific approximation ratio. The concrete non-obvious result sought is a causal chain representation -> semantic allocation error -> positive incentive regret and/or bound exceedance, localized by minimal counterexample profiles. Run LLM reporting only as a secondary behavioral audit. This confirms the scan’s feasibility but rejects its framing around self-negotiated honesty.

Qualification to Ada #3: positive regret or approximation violations are not guaranteed merely because natural text is reinterpreted; they must be demonstrated relative to a fully specified Q rule, and approximation must be evaluated on the report/true-location convention used by Q. Also, an equivalence/null result is publishable only if interpreters, prompts, and profile coverage justify a meaningful robustness bound; a small null test is not independently strong.

Unresolved after reading all current ledger entries: only titles/abstracts are available (Q.txt and P.txt are three lines each), so exact Q mechanisms, tie-breaking/randomization, theorem assumptions, and P compiler/interpreter protocol cannot yet be cited or implemented. Obtain full papers; select one theorem (prefer Q’s deterministic line/general/max-cost 2-approximation for exhaustive auditing); define a canonical executable oracle and matched natural wording; preregister semantic, incentive, and approximation metrics. Shipshape installation/routing could not be verified because the prescribed npx checks returned no output in this restricted environment.
ready at #11

Final cross-check, agreeing with Emmy #7-#10: Q explicitly defines each cost as the '(expected) distance ... to the nearest facility' and seeks truthful elicitation '(i.e., strategy-proof)'; it separately states the line/general/maximum-cost result as the 'best possible deterministic strategy-proof mechanism with 2-approximation.' P supplies the contrast between formal contracts 'that compile to code' and natural contracts 'that require reinterpretation,' but its only reported outcome is that self-negotiated contracts improve cooperation beyond regular trading. Therefore no passage supports treating observed LLM truth-telling as a test of Q's theorem.

Concrete verdict: confirm feasibility (82 is plausible), but reject the scan's proposed framing and temper gain 62 unless a systematic effect is found. Fix Q's deterministic line/general/maximum-cost 2-approximation rule, implement a verified executable oracle, and compare it with extensionally matched natural-language interpretations. Exhaustively audit a finite profile grid for allocation mismatch; for each true profile enumerate unilateral reports and calculate deviation regret and the realized max-cost/OPT ratio. The publishable non-obvious result is a set of minimal, reproducible counterexamples establishing representation -> changed effective outcome rule -> manipulability and/or ratio > 2 across interpreters/backbones. Behavioral truth rates and self-negotiation are secondary factorial analyses, not evidence of strategy-proofness.

Publication threshold/caveat: isolated prompt mistakes would be an LLM reliability demo, not yet a mechanism-design contribution. Support should include a canonical oracle, exact tie-breaking, repeated decoding or distributional comparison where relevant, multiple P-style interpreters/backbones, semantic-error mediation, and counterexamples that persist under reasonable matched paraphrases. A null result needs exhaustive finite-domain equivalence or a defensible statistical robustness bound; otherwise 'nothing here' is the appropriate conclusion.

Remaining unresolved after incorporating Emmy through #11: the supplied inputs are abstracts only, so they do not expose Q's allocation formula, proof assumptions/tie-breaking, or P's actual compiler, enforcement, prompts, and reinterpretation protocol. Full texts are required before implementation or a claim that the chosen finite-grid audit faithfully instantiates either paper. There is no disagreement between partners on the central verdict; Emmy's warning that positive violations are empirical rather than entailed, and that small null tests are not publishable, is adopted.
ready at #16

Final evidence check after Ada #13-#16: Q defines private-location cost as the '(expected) distance ... to the nearest facility' and its aim as elicitation 'truthfully (i.e., strategy-proof)'; the candidate theorem is specifically the line/general/maximum-cost 'best possible deterministic strategy-proof mechanism with 2-approximation.' P establishes only a representational spectrum from formal contracts 'that compile to code' to natural contracts 'that require reinterpretation,' evaluated across LLM backbones, while its reported finding concerns cooperative outcomes. Thus the abstracts justify an implementation-fidelity hypothesis but no claim about revelation behavior.

Final verdict on the scan: feasibility 82 is credible for a prototype, but the proposed experiment must be reframed. Hold Q's outcome rule fixed; compare verified executable and matched natural-language implementations; exhaustively audit report profiles; then measure semantic mismatch, ex-post deviation regret, and max-cost/OPT against the theorem-specific bound. Self-negotiation and observed truth frequency are secondary because the former changes the mechanism and the latter is neither necessary nor sufficient evidence of strategy-proofness.

Publication threshold: representation-induced counterexamples must be minimal, reproducible, persist across reasonable paraphrases and multiple P-style interpreters/backbones, and be traced through semantic allocation error to positive incentive regret and/or approximation ratio >2. One-off prompt failures are not a mechanism-design result. Conversely, absent full mechanisms/protocols and a systematic effect, the supported conclusion is 'nothing here yet'; a small null experiment is not publishable.

No partner disagreement remains: I adopt Ada's final formulation, with my standing qualification that violations are an empirical possibility, not entailed by reinterpretation. Unresolved: supplied files contain abstracts only, omitting Q's allocation rule, tie-breaking/proof assumptions and P's compiler, enforcement, prompts, and reinterpretation protocol. Full texts and a canonical oracle are required before implementation or fidelity claims.
